title: This Bird Fakes a Broken Wing to Save Its Eggs, Then Just Flies Off

scenes.text: This bird's wing looks broken. Watch what happens next.
A fox spots a killdeer on the ground, one wing flared at an awkward angle, crying out. An easy meal.
The bird staggers away from its nest, always just out of reach. The fox follows. And follows.
Then, far enough from the eggs, the wing heals instantly. The killdeer flies off. The fox gets nothing.
Cows and horses get a different act: the killdeer puffs up and charges them, so they don't step on the nest.
Four eggs on bare gravel, defended by pure acting. Now watch that wing again.

description:
The killdeer nests on open gravel, so it protects its four eggs with a performance: it flares a wing at an awkward angle, cries out and staggers away, luring raccoons, foxes and coyotes from the nest before flying off unharmed.
For big grazing animals like cows and horses it switches tactics, puffing up and charging so they do not trample the nest.
Have you ever seen a bird pull the broken-wing act?
thumbnail_text: THE BROKEN WING IS A LIE
subject: killdeer bird
first_comment: Killdeer chicks hatch on gravel roofs too, and some have survived seven-storey drops on their first day. What is the best animal bluff you have seen?
